rows.question: Which company built the spacecraft Michael Collins stayed in while the first Moon landing took place?
rows.answer:
North American Aviation built it.

Michael Collins stayed in lunar orbit aboard Columbia during the landing: [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

Columbia was Apollo 11's command module: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Apollo 11's command module was Columbia (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".

That module was built by North American Aviation: [[command-service-module]] "[stated] Built by North American Aviation (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

North American Aviation was also the prime contractor for the command and service module: [[north-american-aviation]] "[stated] Prime contractor for the Apollo command and service module (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)".

rows.question: For about how long were the heaters of the tank that later exploded on Apollo 13 run on ground power before launch, and what did the investigating board say started the explosion?
rows.answer:
The tank's heaters ran on ground power for about eight hours, and the board said an electrically started fire started the explosion.

- **Heater time:** Before launch, oxygen tank No. 2 was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Before launch it was emptied by running its heaters on 65-volt ground power for about eight hours (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"
- **Board finding:** The Apollo 13 Review Board traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2. [[apollo-13-review-board]] "[stated] Traced the explosion to an electrically started fire in oxygen tank No. 2 (src: Apollo 13 Review Board report, 2026-10-24)"
- **Switch failure:** The board's report called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Called the switch failure a serious oversight in which all parties share (src: Michigan Daily 1970 coverage, 2026-10-24)"
- **Why the switches failed:** The switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Its thermostatic switches were built to a 1962 specification for 28 volts DC (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)" The heater specification was revised to 65 volts in 1965, but the switches were not changed. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] The heater specification was revised in 1965 to 65 volts but the switches were not changed (src: Moonport SP-4204, 2026-10-24)"

- The speech date: [[john-f-kennedy]] "[stated] Gave the 'We choose to go to the Moon' speech at Rice University on 1962-09-12 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The 63-day figure is my own calculation from those two dates.

rows.question: The landing site described in the Apollo 11 Mission Report's powered-descent section was named by an astronaut. What was first about the Gemini flight he commanded, and when was it?
rows.answer:
The landing site is Tranquility Base, and Neil Armstrong named it. The powered-descent section describes the landing there.

[[tranquility-base]] "[stated] Named by Neil Armstrong at touchdown: Houston, Tranquility Base here, the Eagle has landed (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"

The Gemini flight he commanded, Gemini 8, was the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit. It flew in 1966.

[[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

The notes give only the year, 1966, and no month or day.

rows.question: The astronaut who caught German measles before Apollo 13 set off a crew swap. What office did the astronaut brought in by that swap later win, and what happened?
rows.answer:
The astronaut who caught German measles was Charlie Duke. [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Caught German measles from a friend's 3-year-old son about three weeks before the Apollo 13 launch (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". rows.question: How many years separate Neil Armstrong's Gemini 8 command and John Young's command of the first Space Shuttle flight?
rows.answer:
The two commands are 15 years apart. Armstrong commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, and Young commanded STS-1 in 1981 (1981 − 1966 = 15).

- [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] Earlier commanded Gemini 8 in 1966, the first docking of two spacecraft in orbit (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"
- [[john-young]] "[stated] Commanded STS-1 in 1981, the first Space Shuttle flight (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: List every Apollo mission in the brain that launched with a crew, with its launch date.
rows.answer:
Four Apollo missions in the brain launched with a crew. Apollo 1 is not one of them, because it never launched.

- **Apollo 8** launched on 1968-12-21. [[apollo-8]] "[stated] Launched 1968-12-21 with Frank Borman, Jim Lovell and Bill Anders (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
- **Apollo 11** launched on 1969-07-16. [[apollo-11]] "[stated] Launched 1969-07-16 from Kennedy Space Center Launch Complex 39A (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **Apollo 13** launched on 1970-04-11. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **Apollo 16** launched on 1972-04-16. [[apollo-16]] "[stated] Launched 1972-04-16 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" Its crew was John Young, Ken Mattingly and Charlie Duke. [[apollo-16]] "[stated] Crew was John Young, Ken Mattingly and Charlie Duke (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

Apollo 1 was a cabin fire during a launch rehearsal on 1967-01-27, so it has no launch date. [[apollo-1]] "[stated] A cabin fire during a launch rehearsal test on 1967-01-27 killed Gus Grissom, Ed White and Roger Chaffee (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

The brain also mentions Apollo 17 as the last crewed lunar mission, in December 1972. [[apollo-program]] "[stated] Apollo 17 in December 1972 was the last crewed lunar mission (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)" It gives no exact launch date for Apollo 17, so I left it out of the list.

rows.question: Which people does the brain explicitly name as walking on the Moon?
rows.answer:
The brain explicitly names three people as walking on the Moon: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin and Charlie Duke.

- **Neil Armstrong:** He was the "First person to step onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC" [[neil-armstrong]] "[stated] First person to step onto the lunar surface on 1969-07-21 UTC (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".
- **Buzz Aldrin:** He was "the second person to walk on the Moon" [[buzz-aldrin]] "[stated] Lunar module pilot of Apollo 11 and the second person to walk on the Moon (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)".
- **Charlie Duke:** He "Walked on the Moon as Apollo 16 lunar module pilot" [[charlie-duke]] "[stated] Walked on the Moon as Apollo 16 lunar module pilot (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)".

The brain gives the total as twelve, but it doesn't name the other nine. [[apollo-program]] "[stated] Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"

Two other people are not stated to have walked on the Moon:
- **Michael Collins:** He stayed in lunar orbit aboard Columbia during the landing. [[michael-collins]] "[stated] Stayed in lunar orbit aboard the command module Columbia during the landing (src: NASA Apollo 11 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **John Young:** His note says he commanded Apollo 16 but not that he walked on the Moon. [[john-young]] "[stated] Commander of Apollo 16 (src: NASA biography, 2026-10-24)"

rows.question: Put every 1970 date the brain records for Apollo 13 in order, with what happened on each.
rows.answer:
Here are the 1970 dates the brain records for Apollo 13, in order. I've rewritten the citations to include the "[stated]" tag that starts each fact line.

- **1970-04-06:** Physicals took place. Blood tests from them showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] Blood tests from the 1970-04-06 physicals showed Ken Mattingly had no rubella immunity (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-10:** The crew swap was decided and announced. [[rubella-crew-swap]] "[stated] The swap was decided at a KSC management meeting and announced at a press conference on 1970-04-10 (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)". Swigert replaced Mattingly as command module pilot. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Command module pilot is Jack Swigert (was Ken Mattingly, changed 1970-04-10 by KSC management meeting) (src: NASA history Apollo 13 measles article, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-11:** Apollo 13 launched. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Launched 1970-04-11 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-13:** Oxygen tank No. 2 exploded. [[oxygen-tank-2]] "[stated] Exploded on 1970-04-13, about 56 hours into the flight (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)". The same day, Mission Control's abort decision changed the mission goal to a safe return to Earth. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Mission goal became a safe return to Earth (was a lunar landing at Fra Mauro, changed 1970-04-13 by Mission Control abort decision) (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **1970-04-17:** The crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down. [[apollo-13]] "[stated] Crew used the lunar module Aquarius as a lifeboat and splashed down on 1970-04-17 (src: NASA Apollo 13 mission page, 2026-10-24)"
- **June 1970 (no day given):** The Review Board report was published. [[apollo-13-review-board-report]] "[stated] Published in June 1970 (src: NASA history, 2026-10-24)"
